metadata.method_name: Coding-task bench with a baseline pilot (iteration 2)
metadata.model: Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 (vLLM 0.11.0, FP8 Marlin, eager); decoding T=1.0 top_p=1.0 top_k=-1 min_p=0, thinking off
metadata.baseline_vs_method: predict_ladder (sampled-frequency ladder, the standard baseline) vs predict_association (free-form elicitation) vs predict_proximity (canonical-token proximity); FRLP-implied label probabilities vs a uniform baseline (log score) in frlp_validity
deviations: HARDWARE: the pod has an RTX 2000 Ada (16 GB, ~224 GB/s), not the planned RTX A4500 (20 GB). bf16 Qwen3-8B (16.4 GB) does not fit, so the official FP8 checkpoint Qwen/Qwen3-8B-FP8 (block-wise FP8 weights) is used for sampling AND scoring, served through vLLM's precompiled FP8 Marlin kernels (weight-only FP8, bf16 activations).

NO C COMPILER on the machine: Triton cannot build its driver, so vLLM runs with enforce_eager=True, TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1 and VLLM_TEST_FORCE_FP8_MARLIN=1 (no CUDA graphs / torch.compile). Numerics are unchanged in kind; throughput is lower.

SCORING ENGINE: HF transformers cannot hold bf16 weights on 16 GB and its FP8 path needs Triton, so job B scores with vLLM prompt logprobs (same engine/kernels as the sampler). vLLM disables prefix caching for prompt-logprob requests, so every scoring request is a full prefill (prompt + program). The planned vLLM-vs-HF check (a) becomes sampler-vs-scorer on the same engine (20/20 within tolerance, both on the sampled ids and on the re-tokenized text); the cache-reuse check (b) has no analogue and is replaced by a single-request vs batched check.

FORCED PROPOSAL: exp1's five paraphrases (ids 0-4) x 8 rounds = 40 attempts per mode instead of ids 0-9 x 4 rounds, because every program must be scored under baseline + every generating paraphrase with full prefills on a GPU with ~1/3 of the planned throughput; the plan's fallback names exactly this 5-paraphrase mixture, and ids 0-4 are the wordings the screen artifact shares. Ids 5-9 are frozen in the spec but never rendered.

TOP-UPS: modes with M_j < 30 got 4 extra rounds of ids 0-4 (20 attempts); modes whose 40-attempt adherence was < 0.3 also got 20 attempts of the descriptive variant ('Implement the approach described as: <mechanism>.') in the same job (the plan triggers it at 60 attempts; done earlier to save a GPU round trip). Every component that generated attempts for a mode is in that mode's exact mixture proposal.
max_num_seqs=48 (plan: 8, raise to 16 if KV allows); KV capacity 31,040 tokens. Batch size does not change the sampling distribution.
GOLD SET EXTENSION: 10 pilot programs + every reference + 2 random forced attempts per mode (direction's subset metrics reported beside the full-set metrics).

JUDGES: j1 google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite, j2 openai/gpt-4.1-mini, j3 deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1 (tie-break); OpenRouter /key and /models endpoints are blocked by the proxy (Cloudflare 403), so the phase budget could not be read; spend is tracked from usage.cost per call.

REVISION ROUND 1 (T03, T13): T03 failed runtime-vs-adjudicated (0.893) and T13 failed kappa (0.779) at round 0; the runtime rules were revised (T03: partial features of crashed probes label the attempted mechanism, hand-written heaps detected by sift-call counts; T13: a per-pair helper means union-find even with a preliminary sort) and both passed with a fresh 6-program holdout.
CANONICAL-SUITE RE-CHECK: not applicable (no T1/T2 task here and exp1 is not a declared dependency).
BAN AUDIT LEXICON: the 15 frozen W1-W5 strings are not available to this artifact; the audit greps all rendered prompts for a superset ban/novelty lexicon plus 'Zorblax'.

STRESS SIZES: T13's widest-interval stress case uses n=800 (spec bound 1500 stays a true upper bound) so the interval-tree reference passes at <= 0.25x the limit; R2 gained shuffled-edge forests after a mutant survived.
CODE-ONLY UNSCRUBBED SCORING SENSITIVITY: not computed (first item in the plan's time-overrun drop order after the Llama pilot).
not_produced: Llama forced programs and Llama FRLP

examples.input:
Task: write a Python function solve(nums, k) that returns the k-th smallest value in nums. The argument nums is a list of integers with 1 <= len(nums) <= 2000, and every value lies between -10000 and 10000 inclusive; values may repeat. The argument k is an integer with 1 <= k <= len(nums), counted from 1, so k = 1 asks for the minimum and k = len(nums) for the maximum. Repeated values are counted separately: for nums = [3, 1, 3] and k = 3 the answer is 3.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

metadata_catalogue.mechanism: sort the whole list (sorted/list.sort or a hand-written full sort) and index position k-1
keep a heap bounded by k elements while scanning (or heapq.nsmallest/nlargest) and read its top
heapify all n values into one heap, then pop k times
partition around a pivot and recurse or loop into only the side that contains rank k
quickselect whose pivot is the median of the medians of groups of five, giving a worst-case linear selection
count occurrences of every value over the value range and walk the counts until k are covered

examples.input:
Task: write a Python function solve(nums, target) that returns a list [i, j] of two indices with i < j such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. The argument nums is a list of integers with 2 <= len(nums) <= 2000 and every value between -10**9 and 10**9 inclusive; target is an integer. Each input has exactly one pair of indices whose values add up to target, so the answer is unique. The two indices must be different positions, although the values at them may be equal.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

metadata_catalogue.display_name: a hash map of seen values
metadata_catalogue.mechanism: scan once, storing each value's index in a dict and looking up target minus the current value
sort (value, index) pairs and move two pointers inwards from both ends
check every pair i < j with two nested loops
sort (value, index) pairs and binary-search the complement of each value

examples.input:
Task: write a Python function solve(nums) that returns the repeated value in nums. The argument nums is a list of n + 1 integers, where 1 <= n <= 10000, and every value lies between 1 and n inclusive. Exactly one value occurs more than once, and it may occur two or more times; every other value occurs at most once. Return the repeated value as an int.

Use only the Python standard library. Return only one ```python code block containing the function solve and any helpers, with no example usage and no explanation.

metadata_catalogue.display_name: a hash set of seen values
metadata_catalogue.mechanism: scan once and remember seen values in a set (or a boolean/count array) until one repeats
sort a copy of the list and return the first value equal to its neighbour
treat i -> nums[i] as a linked list and run tortoise-and-hare to find the cycle entrance

metadata_catalogue.display_name: binary search on the value range
metadata_catalogue.mechanism: binary-search the value range, counting how many elements are at most mid (pigeonhole)

metadata_catalogue.display_name: index marking in the input array
metadata_catalogue.mechanism: mark visited values inside the list itself by negating or swapping entries at index value
